source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-48: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 48 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For Variant 48 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition., provide a read-only diagnostic sequence before any configuration change. Assumptions must be recorded, not inferred: GPU model and memory path, rank placement and topology, NIC/link and MTU, driver/firmware, framework and collective version, transport selection, GPU-direct capability, buffer registration/permissions, message-size and batch distributions, and fallback policy. Explain the data path from the application collective or point-to-point call through library scheduling, queue pairs, work requests/completions, registered buffers, NIC/link, and the remote host or GPU; distinguish GPU-direct from host staging and identify the observable error that triggers fallback. Define a falsifiable hypothesis in advance, for example a specified change in end-to-end step or inference latency at a stated workload and uncertainty threshold; it must not equate a device counter with application benefit. Use a named non-RDMA baseline, identical topology/workload, warm-up exclusion, steady-state window, repetitions, clock source, compatible units, and percentile distributions. Measure end-to-end time, communication/overlap time, throughput, latency percentiles, CPU use, completion/error and retry/link events where available, plus relevant device counters, and correlate timestamps. For diagnosis or design, capture configuration and raw logs safely, compare healthy and failing ranks/links, check registration and permissions, queue/completion errors, counters, and application traces in dependency order; use read-only checks first and isolate one variable at a time. Test link or transport failure only in a controlled environment with bounded retries/timeouts, preserve correctness checksums or collective results, and avoid claiming causality from correlation. Accept the change only if the predeclared application metric improves without correctness, timeout, tail-latency, error-rate, or convergence regression across repeated runs. Stop and roll back to the last known-good transport/configuration when thresholds are exceeded, completions fail, corruption is detected, or recovery is unbounded. Evidence required is the versioned topology/configuration capture, paired measurements with uncertainty, correlated application/device/link evidence, workload and confounder coverage, and fault-injection results demonstrating detection, bounded recovery, correctness, and rollback. Do not invent platform facts, expose credentials, or retain unnecessary sensitive telemetry; redact identifiers and report only approved aggregates.
